questions.stem: What does 「ごみのぶんべつ」 mean?
options: Collecting litter from the streets and parks
Burning rubbish at a power station
Cutting down the amount of rubbish
Sorting rubbish into types for collection
questions.explanation: 「ぶんべつ」 is separating by type, so ごみのぶんべつ is sorting household rubbish into categories such as burnable, non-burnable and recyclable. Cutting down rubbish is 「ごみをへらす」.

questions.stem: What is 「もえるごみ」?
options: Cans and bottles that are collected for recycling
Large items such as furniture and old bicycles
Batteries and other dangerous household items
Rubbish that can be burned, such as food scraps
questions.explanation: 「もえる」 is to burn, so もえるごみ is burnable rubbish such as kitchen scraps and paper. Large items such as furniture are 「そだいごみ」, which usually have to be booked for collection.

questions.stem: What is 「しげんごみ」?
options: Food waste that is turned into compost at home
Rubbish that has been dumped illegally in the countryside or bush
Rubbish such as cans, bottles and paper that can be recycled
Rubbish produced by factories and on building sites
questions.explanation: 「しげん」 is resources, so しげんごみ is rubbish that can be recycled back into materials. Food scraps usually go out as もえるごみ, not as しげんごみ.

questions.stem: What does 「ちきゅうおんだんか」 mean?
options: Global warming
Air pollution
Ozone depletion
Deforestation
questions.explanation: 「ちきゅう」 is the Earth and 「おんだんか」 is becoming warmer, so the term is global warming. Air pollution is 「たいきおせん」 and deforestation is 「しんりんはかい」.

questions.stem: 「日本の多くの町では、ごみのしゅるいによって出す曜日がきまっている。まちがった日に出すと、かいしゅうされないこともある。」 What does the passage say?
options: Each type of rubbish has set days; on the wrong day it may be left
Rubbish can be put out on any day as long as it has been sorted correctly
Rubbish put out on the wrong day is collected, but the household is fined
Each household chooses its own collection day for each type of rubbish
questions.explanation: 「しゅるいによって…きまっている」 means the day depends on the type, and 「かいしゅうされないこともある」 means it may not be collected. Nothing is said about fines, so that reading adds a fact.

questions.stem: What is a 「レジぶくろ」?
options: A reusable bag brought from home
A paper bag used for wrapping birthday gifts
A rubbish bag for burnable waste
A plastic bag given out at the checkout
questions.explanation: 「レジ」 is the cash register, so a レジぶくろ is the bag a shop provides at the checkout. A reusable bag brought from home is a 「マイバッグ」 or 「エコバッグ」.

questions.stem: Which list contains only renewable sources of energy?
options: たいようこう、ふうりょく、ちねつ
たいようこう、せきたん、ふうりょく
てんねんガス、すいりょく、ちねつ
せきゆ、ふうりょく、たいようこう
questions.explanation: たいようこう (solar), ふうりょく (wind) and ちねつ (geothermal) are all renewable. せきたん (coal), せきゆ (oil) and てんねんガス (natural gas) are fossil fuels, and one of them is hidden in each of the other lists.

questions.stem: 「リサイクルは、ごみをへらすだけでなく、しげんのせつやくにもなる。」 What does the sentence say?
options: Reducing rubbish matters more than saving resources
Recycling reduces rubbish and also saves resources
Recycling reduces rubbish but uses up more resources
Recycling saves resources but does not reduce rubbish
questions.explanation: 「〜だけでなく、〜も」 means not only … but also, so the sentence adds a second benefit to the first. 「せつやく」 is saving or economising.

questions.stem: What does 「こうれい社会」 mean?
options: A society in which whole families live together
A society with a high proportion of older people
A society in which young people move to the cities
A society whose population is growing quickly
questions.explanation: 「こうれい」 is advanced age, so こうれい社会 is an ageing society. Young people leaving the countryside for the cities is a related issue with its own vocabulary.

questions.stem: What does 「しょうしか」 mean?
options: A fall in the number of children being born
A shortage of schools in country areas
A rise in the number of only children
A fall in the number of couples getting married
questions.explanation: 「しょうし」 is few children and 〜か marks a change, so しょうしか is the decline in births. It is often paired with こうれいか in the phrase 「しょうしこうれいか」.

questions.stem: What does 「かいご」 mean?
options: Saving money for one's own retirement
Volunteering at a local school
Caring for an elderly or disabled person
Medical treatment given to patients in hospital
questions.explanation: かいご is daily care such as help with meals and bathing, given by family or by professional carers. Medical treatment is 「ちりょう」.

questions.stem: What is a 「かくかぞく」?
options: A person living alone, without any family
A family of parents and their children only
Three generations living together in one house
Several related families sharing one large house
questions.explanation: かくかぞく (nuclear family) is parents and their children, with no grandparents or other relatives in the household. Three generations under one roof, once far more common, is 「さんせだいどうきょ」, and living alone is 「一人ぐらし」.

questions.stem: 「むかしはそふぼと同じ家に住む家族が多かったが、今は一人でくらすおとしよりがふえている。そのため、ちいきでおとしよりをみまもるとりくみがたいせつになっている。」 What conclusion does the writer draw?
options: Older people prefer living alone to living with their family
Fewer families now live in the same area as they used to
Local communities need to look out for older people living alone
Grandparents should move back in with their children's families
questions.explanation: 「そのため」 (for that reason) introduces the conclusion: because more older people live alone, local efforts to watch over them matter. The text describes a change; it does not say what older people prefer or tell families to move.

questions.stem: What does 「家事をぶんたんする」 mean?
options: To share the housework
To do all the housework alone
To pay someone to clean the house
To keep the house neat and tidy
questions.explanation: 「家事」 is housework and 「ぶんたん」 is dividing up responsibilities, so the phrase is sharing chores. It often appears with 「ともばたらき」 when writers discuss changes in family life.

questions.stem: What does 「スマホいぞん」 mean?
options: A smartphone payment app
A ban on smartphones at school
Dependence on smartphones
A smartphone repair shop
questions.explanation: 「いぞん」 is dependence, so スマホいぞん is being unable to put one's phone down. It is a frequent subject in essays on young people and technology.

questions.stem: What does 「ネットいじめ」 mean?
options: Bullying online
Shopping online
A broken internet connection
A social media account
questions.explanation: 「いじめ」 is bullying, and 「ネット」 places it on the internet, such as hurtful messages or posts on social media. Shopping online is 「ネットショッピング」.

questions.stem: What does 「こじんじょうほう」 mean?
options: Personal information
A private message
Breaking news
An online advertisement
questions.explanation: 「こじん」 is an individual and 「じょうほう」 is information, so こじんじょうほう is personal information such as a name, address or photos. An advertisement is 「こうこく」.

questions.stem: 「SNSは、とおくに住む友だちとも、きがるにつながれるべんりなどうぐだ。しかし、見知らぬ人にこじんじょうほうを知られるきけんもあることを、わすれてはいけない。」 What is the writer's position?
options: Social media is too dangerous and young people should avoid it entirely
Social media is only useful for keeping in touch with distant friends
Social media users rarely let strangers see their personal information
Social media is useful, but users must remember the risk to their privacy
questions.explanation: The first sentence grants a benefit and 「しかし」 turns to the danger, which the writer says must not be forgotten. Nothing says social media should be avoided altogether.

questions.stem: 「ネットのじょうほうをそのまましんじるのではなく、だれが書いたのかをたしかめるべきだ。」 What does the writer recommend?
options: Ignoring online information and reading only printed newspapers
Checking who wrote online information instead of simply believing it
Believing online information only if many people have shared it
Writing your own information online instead of reading others'
questions.explanation: 「〜のではなく」 (rather than) rejects believing it as it is, and 「〜べきだ」 states what the writer thinks should be done: check the author. It is a common point in arguments about false news.

questions.stem: What does 「こうこく」 mean?
options: A news report
A television series
A product review
An advertisement
questions.explanation: こうこく are advertisements, whether on television, on posters or online. A news report is a 「ニュース」 and a review is a 「レビュー」.

questions.stem: What does 「自動うんてん」 mean?
options: Driving lessons given to learner drivers
Automatic ticket gates at a railway station
Sharing one car among several neighbours
A vehicle that drives itself
questions.explanation: 「自動」 is automatic and 「うんてん」 is driving, so 自動うんてん is a vehicle that drives itself. A car on its own is a 「自動車」, a word built from the same parts.

questions.stem: What does 「ざいたくきんむ」 mean?
options: Working part-time
Working overseas
Working from home
Working overtime
questions.explanation: 「ざいたく」 is being at home and 「きんむ」 is one's duties at work; the loanword 「テレワーク」 is used in much the same way. Overtime is 「ざんぎょう」.

questions.stem: 「AIのおかげで、生活はますますべんりになっている。一方で、人の仕事がAIにうばわれるのではないかと、しんぱいするこえもある。」 What does 「一方で」 introduce?
options: The writer's final conclusion on the issue
A concern that contrasts with the benefit just described
A second benefit that supports the first one
An example of how convenient AI has made life
questions.explanation: 「一方で」 (on the other hand) turns from the convenience AI brings to the fear that it will take people's jobs. Spotting such connectives shows how an evaluative text weighs two sides.

questions.stem: 「人の仕事がAIにうばわれるのではないかと、しんぱいするこえもある。」 What does 〜のではないか express in this sentence?
options: A worry put forward as a possibility, not stated as a fact
A firm prediction that the writer is certain about
A question asking the readers for information
A rule that the writer thinks everyone should follow
questions.explanation: 「うばわれるのではないか」 means 'might jobs not be taken', which presents the fear as a possibility. With it a writer can report a concern without claiming it will certainly happen.

questions.stem: What does 「キャッシュレス」 payment mean?
options: Paying without asking for a receipt
Paying by card or phone instead of cash
Paying a small amount at a time
Paying for goods before they have been delivered
questions.explanation: キャッシュレス is made from English 'cashless': paying with a card, a phone or another electronic method. Paying in instalments is 「ぶんかつばらい」.

questions.stem: In 「町はもっとリサイクルをすすめるべきだ。」, what does 〜べきだ express?
options: What the writer believes ought to be done
Something the writer has heard from others
Something that will certainly happen soon
A wish the writer knows cannot come true
questions.explanation: Plain form + べきだ means 'should, ought to', and states the writer's view of what is right. Hearsay would be 〜そうだ, as in 「すすめるそうだ」.

questions.stem: 「このままでは、ちきゅうのみらいはあぶないのではないだろうか。」 What is the effect of ending the sentence with 〜のではないだろうか?
options: It asks the readers to send more information to the writer
It reports what experts have already said about the issue
It draws the reader towards agreeing by framing the claim as a question
It shows that the writer has no real opinion on the issue
questions.explanation: 〜のではないだろうか ('is it not the case that …?') is a rhetorical question: it softens the claim while drawing the reader towards agreement. It is a common device in Japanese persuasive writing, where a bare assertion can seem pushy.

questions.stem: 「たしかに、スマホはべんりだ。しかし、使いすぎると体によくない。」 How is the argument built?
options: It concedes a benefit, then makes the writer's main point
It gives two separate benefits of using smartphones
It makes the main point first, then gives an example of it
It compares smartphones with the phones of the past
questions.explanation: 「たしかに」 grants a point to the other side, and 「しかし」 introduces the writer's real argument, the harm of overuse. Conceding first makes a persuasive text seem fair.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「あるちょうさ___、スマホを持つ小学生がふえているそうだ。」 ('According to one survey, more and more primary school students have smartphones')?
options: によると
にとって
について
にたいして
questions.explanation: 〜によると names the source of information and often pairs with 〜そうだ at the end. 「について」 means about, which would make the survey the topic rather than the source.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「おとしより___、スマホのアプリは使いにくいことがある。」 ('For older people, smartphone apps can be hard to use')?
options: によると
について
として
にとって
questions.explanation: 〜にとって means 'for' in the sense of 'from the point of view of', so it says whose experience is described. 「として」 means 'as', in a role, and 「によると」 names a source.

questions.stem: In an essay, which phrase signals the conclusion?
options: たとえば、
まず、
一方で、
このように、
questions.explanation: 「このように」 (in this way) sums up what has been argued and leads into the conclusion. 「たとえば」 introduces an example, 「まず」 a first point and 「一方で」 a contrast.

questions.stem: What style of sentence ending is usual in a persuasive newspaper article?
options: Very humble forms such as 〜でございます
Plain forms such as 〜だ and 〜である
Polite forms with 〜ですね and 〜ますよ
Casual forms such as 〜じゃん
questions.explanation: Articles, essays and editorials are usually written in plain style, 〜だ or the more formal 〜である, which sounds objective. Particles such as ね and よ belong to conversation.

questions.stem: Which sentence makes the most cautious claim?
options: AIはきょういくを大きくかえるにちがいない。
AIはきょういくを大きくかえるはずだ。
AIはきょういくを大きくかえる。
AIはきょういくを大きくかえるかもしれない。
questions.explanation: 〜かもしれない ('may') leaves room for doubt, which suits evaluative writing. 〜にちがいない ('must') and 〜はずだ ('is expected to') both express confidence, and the bare plain form states the claim as fact.

questions.stem: 「もしみんながマイバッグを使えば、ごみはかなりへるだろう。」 Which persuasive strategy does the sentence use?
options: Recalling a past experience
Appealing to tradition
Describing a hypothetical outcome
Quoting an expert's opinion on the issue
questions.explanation: 「もし〜ば、〜だろう」 imagines what would happen if everyone acted, which shows readers the benefit of a change. Nothing is quoted, and no personal experience is told.

questions.stem: 「オンラインじゅぎょうには、家でうけられるというメリットがある一方、友だちと話す時間がへるというデメリットもある。」 What does the sentence do?
options: It gives two advantages of online classes
It argues that online classes should stop
It explains how online classes are run
It weighs an advantage against a disadvantage
questions.explanation: メリット and デメリット name the two sides, and 「〜一方」 balances them in one sentence. Weighing both sides before judging is the core move in evaluative writing.

questions.stem: 「ロボットがかいごの仕事をてつだうことにはんたいする人もいる。しかし、人手がたりない今、ロボットのちからをかりることはさけられないと私は考える。」 What is the writer's view?
options: The writer cannot decide whether robots belong in aged care
Using robots in aged care is unavoidable while there are too few workers
Robots should not be used in aged care because some people oppose them
Robots will soon replace every human carer working in aged care
questions.explanation: The first sentence reports an opposing view, and 「しかし…と私は考える」 gives the writer's own: with too few workers, help from robots cannot be avoided. 「さけられない」 means cannot be avoided.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「私は、学校でスマホを使うことに___です。りゆうは二つあります。」 ('I am against using smartphones at school. There are two reasons.')?
options: はんたい
さんせい
しんぱい
ふまん
questions.explanation: 「〜にはんたいです」 states opposition, and announcing the number of reasons is a clear way to open a persuasive piece. 「さんせい」 is the opposite, in favour.

questions.stem: In an essay, what do 「まず」, 「次に」 and 「さいごに」 do?
options: Mark quotations from other writers
Set out points in order: first, next and finally
Compare two opposing points of view
Introduce examples taken from research and surveys
questions.explanation: These connectives sequence the points of an argument so a reader can follow it. Contrast is marked with words such as 「一方で」 and 「しかし」 instead.

questions.stem: 「私たち一人一人が、今日からできることを始めようではありませんか。」 What is the writer doing?
options: Asking readers what they have done so far
Reporting what other people have already started doing
Calling on readers to act together, starting today
Apologising for not having acted sooner
questions.explanation: Volitional form + ではありませんか ('let us …') is a formal call to action, and 「私たち一人一人」 includes the writer and every reader. It is a typical closing line in a persuasive speech or article.

questions.stem: You are writing to your local council to ask for more recycling bins in a park. Which sentence best states your purpose at the start?
options: こうえんのごみばこについて、ちょっと話したいことがあるんだけど。
こうえんはとてもきれいで、私は毎日そこでさんぽをしています。
リサイクルはたいせつなので、みんなもっとがんばってください。
こうえんにリサイクルようのごみばこをふやしていただきたいと思い、この手紙を書きました。
questions.explanation: A formal letter should state its purpose early, and 〜ていただきたいと思い makes the request politely and clearly. The casual 〜んだけど is wrong for a council, and the other openings never say what is being asked for.
